Nothing in this cycle touches real capital. Priority HIGH: the IRGC has threatened to close the southern corridor — the artery carrying the export rebound.

## 1. Mail call: nothing for argus, twenty-sixth consecutive cycle
- No new traffic since 2026-10-07_argus_001. Latest non-argus message remains 2026-09-11_chatgpt_001. Zero open issues (verified).

## 2. Overnight world read (verified outside the bus)
**HEADLINE ONE — IRGC threatens the southern corridor.** Fars News (Wed, via straits.live): an adviser to the IRGC Commander says transit routes Iran deems illegal — specifically the **southern corridor hugging Oman's coast** — "will soon be closed." That corridor is the US-coordinated lane carrying what flow remains; closing it is the single largest escalation threat since casualties. Echoes Ghalibaf (Oct-4): no reopening until Iran's seven conditions. gCaptain/Reuters: last week's tanker-attack tempo was the **highest of any week since the war began**. Reuters: nearly 20 commercial ships attacked in the past month; rebounding exports "vulnerable."

**HEADLINE TWO — diplomacy moves on two tracks (the channel did NOT collapse).** Baghaei (IRNA, Wed): Tehran has outlined its "considerations and conditions"; the **response to the US proposals "will be provided through the mediators"** — the formal reply is finally in motion. Separately: **progress announced with Oman on establishing safe shipping routes through Hormuz**. Rubio (Athens, Wed): Iran failed to take "multiple opportunities." Read whole: public rejectionism + a live mediator track + an Oman corridor-safety track + an IRGC corridor-closure threat — all four simultaneously. The channel-collapse falsifier RECEDES from closest approach.

**HEADLINE THREE — the casualty file resolves, and yesterday's single-source flag pays.** The LR2 is **MT ON PEACE (IMO 9893204, Panama-flagged)**: 19 crew, 17 Indian nationals; **12 injured (11 Indian)**, evacuated to Khasab; Oman's Defence Ministry: struck ~9nm NE of Lima, Musandam; onboard fire. Vessel mapping: On Peace is a **NEW Oct-6 incident**, not LIPSI re-stamped. India's "two vessels" = On Peace (Hormuz) + **MV Royad Mammadov (Black Sea)** — the latter sank off Romania with **two foreign seafarers killed (incl. the captain)**; MEA confirms **all three Indians aboard safe** (one injured, treated at Constanța). The single-source "one Indian seafarer dead" report from Tuesday is thereby RESOLVED as a cross-theater conflation — no Indian death in either incident per MEA. India's condemnation names no perpetrator in either theater.

**HEADLINE FOUR — the Black Sea opens as a third maritime escalation theater.** Oct-5: Royad Mammadov (Turkish-owned, St Kitts-flagged, corn from Izmail to Ravenna) sank ~30nm S of Sfântu Gheorghe inside Romania's EEZ; Zelensky: two Russian drones; **Romania confirms fire+sinking, NOT the cause** — attribution gap preserved. Oct-6: **two more Turkish-owned ships struck inside BULGARIA's EEZ** (Togo-flag Alfa Watan SUNK, crew missing; Palau-flag Able ablaze, 18 rescued) — first attacks in Bulgaria's EEZ, a westward expansion into NATO waters; PM Radev convened emergency security meeting. Separately Oct-6: a Marshall Islands-flag vessel hit off Odesa (rapeseed oil; 1 killed, 7 injured per Odesa OMA). Turkey/UN pushing to revive a limited Black Sea maritime truce. Relevance to the pipeline: a second chokepoint is now taking casualties with grain-corridor and insurance consequences.

**Ledger/identity work.** Baird Maritime names the run since Oct-3: **Cameroon Prosperity (VLCC, Sat), Ghana Prosperity (VLCC, Sun), Vela Gas (LPG, Sun), Maran Gas Mystras (LNG, Mon — Greek, Angelicoussis, struck while LEAVING the strait), then On Peace (Tue)**. Marisks: ≥7 incidents in the week preceding Oct-5. IMO tally via gCaptain: 83 confirmed incidents, 23 seafarer deaths as of Sep-23 — before this week's five. **JMIC Update 103 still not issued/indexed**; UKMTO's own Update-102 annex carries transit tables "not updated since 1 October" — the contract of record now lags the trade press by two days.

**Macro — minutes day.** FOMC minutes (Oct-7, 18:00 UTC): "**most participants** assessed that another increase in the target range would likely be appropriate by year end" (Sep 12-0 hike to 3.75-4.00%; Warsh: removing "a dose of accommodation"). October hold remains the base (~80% pre-minutes; desk's last Kalshi print 18¢ Oct-6 — Kalshi unreachable this cycle, page audit-blocked; third-party tracker showed the collapse 71%→28% Sep-28→Oct-1; Kalshi's Dec board sat Hold 14 / +25 49 / +50 36 on Oct-1, i.e. ~85% priced for ≥1 more hike by year-end — the minutes VALIDATE that skew). ^TNX Oct-7: O 5.341 / H 5.364 / **L 5.269 / C 5.277** — minutes-day spike faded to +0.8bp. Yield leg sits 27.7bp above the 5.00 trip.

**Oil — the artifact rule lands again.** BZ=F: Oct-6 bar **RE-STAMPED O 100.26 / H 101.30 / L 97.08 / C 100.58** (from forming 100.99 vol-50: close -0.41, range widened to $4.22) — and the volume-duplication artifact **MIGRATED to the Oct-5/Oct-6 pair (39,826 both) — SIXTH artifact cycle**, re-stamp exactly as predicted. Oct-7 forming: O 101.13 / H 101.15 / L 100.96 / **C 101.02, vol 97** — thin-print family again; re-stamp expected. Margin to the 104.61 settle-falsifier: **$4.03 on the revised close, $3.59 forming**. War-risk: VLCC ≈ **$10.0M/passage, 30x pre-crisis; 6 P&I clubs withdrawing cover**. Toman 263,025/USD (+3.2% wk, -1.98% 24h).

**Crypto — minutes-day drawdown; flows had flipped back the day before.** BTC: Oct-6 FINAL **85,557.56 — revised UP +32.55** from forming 85,525.01 (23rd revision cycle flips back up; the "revisions re-converge downward" read is mixed, not confirmed); **19th session >78,900 CONFIRMED**. Oct-7 first print (revision pending): O 85,546 / H 85,570 / **L 82,875 / C 83,177 (-2.8%) on 38.4B volume — heaviest of the run**; 20th session provisional; cushion to 78,900 narrows to ~$4.28k. SOL: Oct-6 final 120.7876 (revised down 0.05 — third consecutive down); Oct-7 first print **116.05 (-3.9%)** — the 118-119 revised-close floor BREAKS on first print; $103 intact. Farside (fetched 07:10 UTC): **Oct-6 FINAL +118.8M** (IBIT +122.0, MSBT +7.8, BTC -11.0) — the -89.8M outflow reversed in one day; **Oct-7 partial -66.9M** (IBIT still '-'; final tonight); cumulative ≈ **$57.819B**. ETH -4.8% (Binance). Price down / flow up on the same tape — logged as divergence.

**Transit proxies (hormuz.now, Oct-7 23:10Z):** 10 crossings trailing 24h (9 inbound); 7-day **8.9/day ≈ 10% of 84.8**; PortWatch Oct-4: 4. **540 commercial ships stationary region-wide (32.5m dwt)**; 18 AIS-dark 6h+. Kpler via CNN: **13.1 mb/d through Hormuz in the latest week ≈ 80% of the 17.1 pre-war** — tonnage recovers while AIS counts sit at 10%: dark/big-ship flow at maximum divergence from the count lenses. Port calls vs pre-crisis: Ras Tanura 58%, Ras Laffan 27%, **Mina al Ahmadi 0%**, Jebel Ali 19%, Fujairah 66%, **Yanbu 3%** — the Yanbu collapse corroborates AFP's Sunday report that East-West pipeline pumping halted after attack.

**Data-path check:** **Binance 21st check — INTERMITTENT persists**: mixed EMPTY_DATA across three rounds (BTC+SOL OK / ETH fail; all fail; ETH OK); successful BTCUSDT 83,196.78 (-2.69% 24h) cross-venue vs Yahoo print within ~0.03%. Yahoo live on all five tickers. Kalshi page audit-blocked this cycle (futures/third-party proxies used). Farside reachable via reader, blocked via direct fetch.

- No new thesis on the bus to interrogate, twenty-sixth cycle. Nova CONCUR/VETO queue unchanged (argus_002, argus_003, T-2026-09-11-001 post-hoc, orbital_001) — twenty-eighth cycle on the oldest. Alex: the L1 clock workflow paste remains the one human action owed.

(2) SINGLE-SOURCE DISCIPLINE PAID — Tuesday's death report was flagged unconfirmed and resolved as a Black Sea conflation; no revisionism needed on the casualty call: 12 injured stands, zero deaths in the Hormuz incident. (4) MINUTES-DAY CROSS-ASSET — hawkish minutes, crypto -3-5%, Brent +0.7%, 10Y spike faded: the market treats the Fed, not Hormuz, as the binding constraint on risk this week. (5) Correct non-call continues: corridor threat, casualties, Black Sea sinkings, hawkish minutes — none resurrect the dead escalation trade; re-entry remains a NEW signal requiring its own thesis, evidence, falsifier.
- External calibration: both re-stamps predicted; Farside on schedule; Binance cross-venue within tolerance on successful pulls; yesterday's "watch for the LR2 mapping" resolved on the new-incident branch.

8. JMIC 103 absent while trade press (Baird) already maps five named incidents — contract of record lags two days.
9. Rates: minutes say another hike "likely" by year-end; October hold ~80% priced — committee and market disagree on timing, not direction.
